page: Microsoft Azure E4s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8171M cores with Hyper-Threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz, the x86_64 processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, and AES cryptography. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 66 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the E4s_v3 exhibits modest processing and memory performance. In stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests, the instance falls into the bottom 25% tier for both single-core and multi-core execution. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only operations on cached and uncached blocks, place the system in the bottom 10% to 25% range, with write speeds reaching 18.11 GB/sec. Similarly, database and caching operations, such as Redis SET benchmarks, register in the lower performance brackets. These metrics highlight a clear tradeoff: the instance provides a substantial memory footprint but is constrained by legacy CPU architecture and lower memory throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4s_v3 offers a practical entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high-performance compute resources. The high memory density relative to the vCPU count makes it suitable for hosting small-scale relational databases, caching layers, enterprise applications, and lightweight web serving. It is less suited for compute-heavy tasks like software compilation, complex cryptography, or real-time LLM inference, where its processing limitations would introduce bottlenecks.
